# Refining margins carried the Q3 energy prints; reported Valero purchase of Lyondell's Houston refinery is unverified

**Vintage:** posts 10/30 07:42–14:36 UTC; Q3 results released 10/30 before the US open (XOM, CVX) and 10/30 UK (BP). Relays only; no company release read here.

| Item | As relayed | Status |
|---|---|---|
| BP Q3 | Highest profit in 18 years on refining margins; net debt cut by nearly $10B in the quarter (Javier Blas) | Release not read |
| XOM / CVX Q3 | Both beat, refining profits soared on Gulf and Russia disruption (headline relay) | Releases not read |
| Valero / Lyondell Houston | Valero buying the mothballed Lyondell Houston refinery for $320.5M, restart ~167 kb/d sometime in 2027 (Tom Kloza, OPIS) | **UNVERIFIED.** Search finds only LyondellBasell's 2025 permanent closure of the ~264 kb/d site and a post-2027 plastics-recycling conversion plan. Valero's release not found. |
| Bank forecasts | WSJ survey: 2026 Brent average $90.40 (from $88.13) | Survey not read |
| Spot vs futures | Spot (Dated) Brent fell $6.08 on 10/29 to $114.91, below the front future at $116.19 (Macrostrategy) | Basis claim not checked against a Platts/ICE primary |

**ACTION BRENT:** integrate the refining-margin read into your product-crack frame, and verify or kill the Valero/Lyondell restart claim (a 2027 capacity add would bear on the 3:2:1 crack, boundary #8, which moves to January contracts 11/2). The spot-below-front-month Brent basis is yours to grade.

**INFO HENRY / CARL:** refining margins as an inflation pass-through input. **RED / TERRY (BOARD pull):** VLO is a held line; no position call from WALTER.

**Limits:** every figure is a relay; the Valero item conflicts with the only located record.
